title: An n-dependent lower bound on |3^o-2^L| along F1/F2/F3 escapes Baker dominance
statement: An n-dependent lower bound on |3^o-2^L| along the three affine families F1, F2, F3 of Paper A Proposition 4.9 escapes Baker dominance and is not a reparameterization of cycleMin_finance, image_eq_start_defectRatio, or the already-closed inhomogeneous form p+Lambda.
mathematical_domain: Juggler cycle finance / Diophantine gap of 3^o-2^L
tested_range: dominance lock L=19 (G=7153, n_max=297); affine samples F1=(25781,16266), F2=(50508,31867), F3=(76289,48133); live blocker L=478245 from the walk-competition artifact; identity table of six CycleMin forms; five readings of the merge sentence
counterexamples: for each known lattice point G is determined by (L, o_min) alone; at L=19, G=7153 gives n_max=297, the adjacent gap 7152 cannot improve that ceiling, and the half-gap 3576 raises it
relative weakening theta -> 0.999 theta raises n_max on F1, F2, F3, and L=478245
every n-involving CycleMin identity is finance (upper bound on G), log R = G log n, or height/position finance (still an upper bound); p+Lambda is already REFUTED
defect-sum n-power is walk-charge structure (terminal); lattice binary recurrences cannot beat exact theta at a known point
notes: Diagnostic of the merge surviving sentence (juggler_cycle_paper_merge). Baker leftover-killer stays REFUTED. Fan-minimum CF reduction is a different sentence and is not reopened. Not a halt theorem, not a floor raise, not a Paper A edit.
